I'd make curiosity the dominant human trait, overriding fear, tribalism, and short-term self-interest.

Right now, people are wired to protect their beliefs, status, and immediate comfort even when it means staying ignorant or making terrible long-term decisions. If that wiring flipped so that most humans felt genuine discomfort when they didn't understand something important, and real satisfaction from figuring it out, a lot of the self-inflicted damage would start correcting itself. Science would accelerate, politics would get less delusional, and people might actually try to solve hard problems instead of just arguing about them or pretending they don't exist.

Everything else—poverty, conflict, stagnation—seems downstream of how little most of us actually want to know. Fix the wanting, and the rest becomes a lot more solvable.
